meta.title: Our Holiday Program
meta.textType: functional: a holiday program with a key

paragraphs: On Thursday, April first, the school holiday began. At ten o'clock, Lily, Mia, Leo, and May met at the town library. Nobody wore a school uniform, because it was the first day of the holiday. A big advertisement hung on the notice board next to the door. It was the library's monthly program for the holiday. Lily held a pencil and a small notebook. "Let's read the whole sheet," she said.

The program had a key in a box at the top. "What does level one mean?" asked Leo. "It is for beginners," said May, "and the key shows a star for level one." "A cup means that a snack is included, a roof means indoor, and a sun means outdoor." The cooking course with Chef Lucy is held on Monday, April fifth, Wednesday, April seventh, and Friday, April ninth. It has a star, a cup, and a roof. It costs three hundred baht, and a snack is included. Only twelve places are available. Cartoon drawing is held on Tuesday and Thursday. It has a roof, so it is indoor, and it costs two hundred baht. Football skills with Coach Matt is outdoor, so it has a sun.

At the bottom of the sheet, four free events were listed. "Health Hour with Nurse Jill is on Tuesday, April twentieth, at two o'clock," read Lily. "Music in the Park is on Saturday, April twenty-fourth, at three o'clock." "History Hour with Guide Ann is on Tuesday, April twenty-seventh, at two o'clock." The last event is the M one Open Morning. It is on Friday, May seventh, from nine to eleven in the morning. Under the events, a line said, "The library is closed on Tuesday, April sixth." "It is also closed from Tuesday, April thirteenth to Thursday, April fifteenth." Mia pointed at the closed days. "We cannot come on those days," she said. May wrote the dates in her own notebook.

Lily scanned the program for dates and times. Then she wrote a small timetable. "Which course are you interested in?" she asked. "Cooking is popular, and only twelve places are available," said Mia. "We may not get a place if we wait." "The sign-up desk is behind the door," said May. A small notice on the desk gave information. It said, "Please write your name and a parent's phone number."

The four friends walked to the desk. Lily picked up the pen. First, Lily, Mia, and May wrote their names for cooking. "I cannot cook, but I can draw a pan," said Leo. He wrote his name for cartoon drawing. Then he drew a small pan beside it. "Then you will draw while we cook," said May. "You may draw us, too," said Mia. Lily looked at her timetable and smiled. "The holiday is long, but our days are full," she said.
text.summary: On the first day of the holiday, the four friends read the library's holiday program and its key. They find the dates, the prices, and the closed days, and then they sign up for their courses.
